_comment: Core systems and the full recorded Blaze Art list: 6 systems, 9 characters with Blaze Arts, and 25 named Arts. Art names are grouped by type because the three types fill their meters differently.

_mechanics.blazeTypes: Celestial Wells belong to Mediators, Underworld Arts come from a character's cursed object, and Automaton Arts belong to Automations. No Automaton Arts are recorded in the source yet.
_mechanics.meter: Arts fill a Blaze Meter: half full grants Overblaze, which raises stats and unlocks certain Arts, and a completely full meter triggers a Burst that halves maximum HP for the rest of the battle.
_mechanics.cost: Blaze Arts are paid for with HP instead of weapon durability, and the HP cost varies between Arts.
_mechanics.rewind: Fortuna's Blessing is the turn-rewinding mechanic, supplied as Divine Sand in limited quantity.
_mechanics.clash: Clash replaces the grid with a shared party HP pool, and linking two characters for an action costs Link Points.

systems.name: Free Time
systems.summary: Preparation time before a Main Battle, measured in Turns.
details: One Turn equals six in-game hours, and the deadline before the next chapter battle is expressed as a number of Turns.
Exploring Dagsion covers the Shopping Arcade for weapons and items, weekly access to a training facility, and spectating other teams in the Heroic Games.
Inns are where meals are shared, units rest, time is passed, and support conversations happen; an auto mode can run the chores to build levels and gather resources.

systems.name: Main Battles
systems.summary: The chapter-equivalent stages of the Heroic Games.
details: A stat card previews each Main Battle with information and recommendations for preparing units.
The same card states the Turn limit allowed before the battle has to begin.
Main Battles are staged in the Grand Arena, and the layouts are drawn from historical battles in Dagda's history.

systems.name: Tactical combat
systems.summary: The primary battle system, inherited from the series.
details: Weapon types replace the weapon triangle with individual baseline mechanics.
Combat Arts are available to units that carry the weapon which unlocks them.

systems.name: Clash
systems.summary: The secondary combat system used in dungeons and in specific story events.
details: Closer to a party-based turn-based RPG than a grid battle, used inside dungeons.
The party shares one collective HP total; reducing it to zero forces an evacuation from the dungeon.
The command menu covers Attack, Combat Arts, and a Link command that pairs two characters for an action such as attacking or healing.
Linking is paid for with a separate resource, Link Points.
Combat can be skipped and resolved automatically.

systems.name: Blaze Arts
systems.summary: Character-specific Combat Arts paid for with HP rather than weapon durability.
details: Nine characters have Blaze Arts, and each Art consumes a portion of the user's HP that varies per Art.
Performing Arts fills a Blaze Meter: half full triggers Overblaze, which boosts stats and unlocks certain Arts.
A completely full meter triggers a Burst, which empties the gauge but halves the user's maximum HP for the remainder of the battle.
The three types are Celestial Wells (Mediators), Underworld (cursed object users) and Automaton (Automations).
Celestial Wells fill the gauge even with ordinary attacks and are reduced by cursed weapons; Underworld Arts come from the character's cursed object and are fuelled by them.

systems.name: Fortuna's Blessing
systems.summary: The turn-rewinding mechanic, granted through Divine Sand.
details: Fortuna gives Eshmel a pouch of Divine Sand, which turns back time; the supply is limited in both quantity and how far it reaches.
Each Flame Lord receives a pouch as part of the plan to change their fates, and the handovers happen at different points in the chronology.

Leda receives hers in 1444 during the Cydonia Massacre as she retrieves Obsidian; Cai receives his on 01/24/1449 at a shrine to Fortuna after a pure white Ornius drags him there; Dietrich receives his shortly after arriving in Dagda and allying with Fabio; Theodora receives hers shortly after learning of the attempt to speed up Dyan's coronation.

blazeArts.name: Purifying Flash
blazeArts.effect: Pierces foes with a spear of holy light. Effective against undead.

blazeArts.name: Dragon Strike I
blazeArts.effect: Unleashes force refined within the body as an area attack. Can destroy obstacles.

blazeArts.name: Dragon Strike II
blazeArts.effect: Unleashes force refined within the body as an area attack. Can destroy obstacles.

blazeArts.name: Dragon Strike III
blazeArts.effect: Unleashes force refined within the body as an area attack. Can destroy obstacles.

blazeArts.name: Shining Dragon Strike
blazeArts.effect: Area attacks that damage all foes in range and destroy obstacles; the affected area grows with each tier.

blazeArts.name: Dragon Rotation
blazeArts.effect: Unleashes a spiral of energy. Can destroy obstacles.

blazeArts.name: Underworld Burst
blazeArts.effect: Fires a blast from the gem in his palm for long-range area damage. During Overblaze it leaves Underworld Flames that damage enemies standing on them.

blazeArts.name: Blackfire
blazeArts.effect: Fires a cone of dark fire. During Overblaze it leaves Underworld Flames that damage enemies standing on them.

blazeArts.name: Underworld Inferno
blazeArts.effect: Available only during Overblaze. Fires a blast of dark fire along a straight line with a circular area at the end, leaving Underworld Flames behind.

blazeArts.name: Moving Shadow
blazeArts.effect: Warp up to three spaces after moving, then attack.

blazeArts.name: Stifling Shadow
blazeArts.effect: Warp up to three spaces after moving, immobilising enemies within two spaces.

blazeArts.name: Umbra Calamity
blazeArts.effect: Effect not recorded in the source checked.
blazeArts.note: The source lists this Art without recording what it does yet.

blazeArts.name: Earthen Throw
blazeArts.effect: Pitches a chunk of rock straight at a foe.

blazeArts.name: Earthen Hurl
blazeArts.effect: Lobs a boulder ripped from the ground at an area of enemies.

blazeArts.name: Song of Beasts
blazeArts.effect: Summons a Demonic Beast. Once per map.

blazeArts.name: Song of Madness
blazeArts.effect: Effect not recorded in the source checked.
blazeArts.note: The source lists this Art without recording what it does yet.

blazeArts.name: Song of Passion
blazeArts.effect: Grants Strength +4 and Magic +4 to all allies in range for one turn; upgradable for larger boosts.

blazeArts.name: Song of Icewater
blazeArts.effect: Grants Defence +4 and Resistance +4 to all allies in range for one turn; upgradable for larger boosts.

blazeArts.name: Song of Abjuring
blazeArts.effect: Grants effectiveness against undead to all allies in range for one turn.

blazeArts.name: Collapsing Curse
blazeArts.effect: Inflicts Numb for one combat or one turn, halving Hit. The area grows during Overblaze.

blazeArts.name: Slowing Curse
blazeArts.effect: Inflicts Slow for one combat or one turn, halving attack speed. The area grows during Overblaze.

blazeArts.name: Unlucky Curse
blazeArts.effect: Inflicts Jinx for one combat or one turn, halving Luck. The area grows during Overblaze.

blazeArts.name: Ruler's Awakening
blazeArts.effect: Grants Hit +50 until the next phase; the unit can attack after using it.

blazeArts.name: Flash Awakening
blazeArts.effect: Grants Protection +10 until the unit's next phase; the unit can attack after using it.

blazeArts.name: Reason Awakening
blazeArts.effect: Grants Resistance +10 until the unit's next phase; the unit can attack after using it.
